chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, peace be upon him:

Concerning a man who wished to testify regarding a woman to whom he was not related as a maḥram: is it permissible for him to testify about her from behind a curtain and hear her speech, if two just witnesses testify that she is so-and-so daughter of so-and-so who is asking you to bear witness, and that this is her speech? Or is testimony about her not permissible until she comes forth and he verifies her with his own eyes?
So he, peace be upon him, wrote: "She should cover her face with a niqab and appear before the witnesses, if Allah wills."

key_terms.السِّتْرِ: a covering or curtain separating the woman from the witness
key_terms.امْرَأَةٍ: a woman who is the subject of the testimony
key_terms.بِمَحْرَمٍ: as a maḥram, meaning a person with whom marriage is permanently forbidden
key_terms.تَتَنَقَّبُ: she covers her face with a niqab
key_terms.عَدْلَانِ: two just witnesses whose reliability is legally recognized
key_terms.لِلشُّهُودِ: for the witnesses, meaning before those giving or establishing testimony
key_terms.يَشْهَدَ: to give testimony or bear witness in a legal matter

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islamic law to testify regarding a non-maḥram woman from behind a curtain based only on her voice?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal question about establishing testimony concerning a woman who is not a maḥram to the witness. The Imam عليه السلام rules that she should appear before the witnesses while veiled with a niqab, indicating the need for visual identification in a manner consistent with modesty.
